### ACT-302: Root `deno.lock` v5 → v3 restoration per Catalog #58 runbook (third lockfile-version firing this session).

Restored root `deno.lock` from `"version": "5"` to `"version": "3"` per Catalog #58 (`docs/ai-failure-modes.md` lines 305-312) runbook. The v5 had been sitting red across multiple commits because prior REVISION-FIX prompts carried the stop condition "do NOT touch lockfiles" — intended to prevent INTRODUCING v5 mid-build, but the framing conflated "don't write v5" with "don't touch the lock at all" and blocked the RESTORATION of an already-v5 lock. Corrected framing: a lock LANDING at v5 is the violation; restoring it to v3 IS the fix and MUST happen in the same commit. **Regen environment:** sandbox default Deno 2.6.10 is the v5 WRITER (using it re-triggers the bug per Catalog #58); explicitly installed pinned Deno 1.46.3 (the CI-matched version) to `/tmp/deno` via `curl https://github.com/denoland/deno/releases/download/v1.46.3/deno-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.zip`, ran `rm deno.lock && /tmp/deno cache --lock=deno.lock --lock-write <strong-evidence.yml lines 92-104 entrypoints>` (the 11 `scripts/check-*.ts` gate scripts + `supabase/functions/_shared/longshort-verifiers/longshort-verifiers_test.ts`). Post-regen `head -2 deno.lock` = `"version": "3"`; a re-run `/tmp/deno cache --lock=deno.lock scripts/check-paper-only-url.ts` did NOT rewrite (proves the lock is stable under 1.46.3). **STEP-B verification gate (the asymmetry-mandated check — root regen against config-less entrypoints re-resolves):** results = **0 version changes, 0 added, 59 dropped**. Per Catalog #58 line 308 the gate is on CHANGED versions only — gate (a) financial-path-reach is vacuously satisfied (0 changed); gate (b) declared-range-bound is vacuously satisfied (0 changed, 0 added, no major bumps, no new top-level deps). Belt-and-suspenders spot-check on 13 sampled dropped frontend deps (`@radix-ui`, `@playwright/test`, `@sentry/react`, `react-router-dom`, `@tanstack/react-query`, `tailwindcss`, `vite`, `vitest`, `@eslint/js`, `lovable-tagger`, `@fontsource`, `jsdom`, `@yu7400ki/zstd-wasm`) — `rg` reach under `supabase/functions/_shared/longshort-combiner/` + `supabase/functions/_shared/longshort-signals/` + `training/` = **0 for all 13** (all dropped entries are frontend/tooling deps unreached from any Deno entrypoint; they were carried into the v5 lock by an earlier broader sandbox cache pass that included frontend code, which `deno cache` against the strong-evidence entrypoints correctly drops — per Catalog #58 "accuracy gains, NOT losses; re-added automatically if later imported"). `supabase/functions/deno.lock` BYTE-UNTOUCHED (already v3; not part of the regen). Gate-0a (`deno run --allow-read scripts/check-lockfile-versions.ts`) now exits 0: `CLEAN — both lockfiles at version "3"`. The 26 combined tests across `scripts/check-lockfile-versions_test.ts` (14) + `scripts/check-paper-only-url_test.ts` (12, includes the ACT-301-area INC-77 SCAN_ROOT-expansion fixes) all green under CI's exact permission set with the new v3 lock. Catalog #58 updated with this firing (third lockfile-version firing, plus the two permission-axis firings = five total sandbox-vs-CI divergence firings this session). NO `.ts` source change, NO migration, NO cron, NO `.yml` change, NO functions-lock touch, NO fire.

### ACT-301: Regime price-history lookback widened 730 → 810 calendar days (insufficient-history fix from 2026-06-23 manual chain fire).

Operator manually fired the regime → assemble → rank chain for `as_of=2026-06-23` tonight (Gate-3.0 sanctioned operator-invoke pattern, ~17h ahead of the first scheduled 22:45 UTC regime cron). Step 1 (`longshort-spy-regime-compute-manual`, correlation_id `2ee55801-7380-4196-9dbc-fb2cf8a3c6ad`) returned `outcome:"failed_insufficient_history"`, `bar_count:501`, `failure_reason:"regime_data_insufficient_history"`. Steps 2 and 3 cascaded correctly: assemble (`9dbb50de-b047-4e31-bedc-718508f02891`) returned `regime_data_unavailable_at_assemble`; rank (`bd84f651-c247-45ba-9327-62ac0bcb004c`) returned `no_included_vectors`. The fail-loud chain behaved exactly as designed — typed `null` on insufficient history (no fabricated regime value), clean propagation, every response carrying its precise typed reason. The only defect was the lookback constant. **Root cause:** `REGIME_PRICE_HISTORY_LOOKBACK_DAYS=730` calendar days × (252/365.25) ≈ 504 trading days — at ZERO margin against the `REGIME_24M_MIN_BARS=504` requirement. Market holidays (~9/yr, ~18 over a 2-yr window) push the trailing trading-bar count under 504; Polygon returned 501 (three short — the holiday shortfall). **Fix:** widened `REGIME_PRICE_HISTORY_LOOKBACK_DAYS` from 730 to 810 calendar days in `supabase/functions/_shared/longshort-signals/market-regime/regime-orchestrator.ts` (≈ 559 trading-day theoretical → ~55-bar margin; absorbs the holiday shortfall in any 2-yr window). The 126-bar vol window (`REGIME_VOL_6M_MIN_BARS`) is amply covered by the same fetch. `REGIME_24M_MIN_BARS=504` UNCHANGED (correct per DEC-066 §(f) / Daniel-Moskowitz 2016, JFE 122(2)). `DEFAULT_PRICE_HISTORY_LOOKBACK_DAYS=400` UNCHANGED (Signal #6's window — different signal). Updated `regime-orchestrator_test.ts` (730 → 810) and added a `>= 774` floor assertion so any future narrowing back below the 6%-holiday-margin threshold trips a test (regression prevention for the 501<504 class). No fetcher change, no schema, no cron change, no `.yml`. **Catch-window value, concretely realized:** had the operator not fired manually tonight, the scheduled 22:45 UTC cron would have hit the same shortfall for `as_of=2026-06-24`, producing a second consecutive no-book day (2026-06-23 assembler already fail-louded at 23:35 by design — no regime row that date since the regime cron was armed at 02:51 UTC). Now: ~17 hours to deploy the fix + manually re-fire `as_of=2026-06-23` before the scheduled cron, so tomorrow's scheduled fire runs against a corrected constant on its first attempt. **Operator follow-up (out-of-scope for this Lovable edit):** Lovable cannot deploy edge functions; the constant is bundled into `longshort-spy-regime-compute-manual` (and the scheduled `longshort-spy-regime-compute`), so the fix MUST be redeployed by the operator before any manual re-fire will pick up the widened lookback. After deploy: operator re-fires the three-step chain for `as_of=2026-06-23` (regime → assemble → rank); Lovable verifies the (c) triplet (regime rows under `__MARKET__`, assemble emits no `regime_data_unavailable_at_assemble`, rank produces non-zero long/short with `ranker_source="count_normalized_fallback"`). NO migration, NO cron arming, NO Lovable fire.

The supervisor's prompt specified the GRANT pattern verbatim; surfaced here per §22.8.5 rather than altered unilaterally. If the supervisor prefers an explicit `REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC` in a follow-up corrective, the gate would remain the load-bearing element either way. |

| **STEP A anchors (verbatim)** | (a) `polygon-price-history-fetcher.ts:135` — `fetchPriceHistory(ticker: string, as_of: Date, lookbackDays: number = DEFAULT_PRICE_HISTORY_LOOKBACK_DAYS): Promise<DailyBar[] \| null>`; 404 → `null` typed-absence; non-2xx / parse / timeout → `SignalComputationError` throw. `DailyBar = { ts: string; close: number }` adjusted via `adjusted=true`. (c) `combiner_forward_returns` PK = `(operator_id, source_table, variant, seed_as_of_date, ticker, horizon_td)`; CHECKs: `horizon_td ∈ {1,5,20}`, `side ∈ {long,short}`, `source_table ∈ {combiner_book, combiner_book_shadow}`, `price_source_status ∈ {success, polygon_404, fetch_error}`, typed-absence `((status='success' AND raw NOT NULL AND signed NOT NULL AND horizon_close_date NOT NULL) OR (status<>'success' AND raw IS NULL AND signed IS NULL))`. (d) `grep -n "live_gated" docs/decisions/DEC-059-dw109-resolution-rule.md` → lines 28 + 34 confirm the live-book label is `live_gated`. (e) `combiner_book` columns: `(operator_id, as_of_date, side, rank_within_side, ticker, score, ranker_source, computed_at)` — NO `variant` column (job stamps `LIVE_VARIANT_LABEL='live_gated'`); `combiner_book_shadow` has `variant`. (f) `shadow-ranker-orchestrator.ts:308-330` — chunked UPSERT with `UPSERT_CHUNK_SIZE=500` and `computed_at = as_of.toISOString()`; manual handler dual-audit envelope (`manual_triggered` → `manual_completed`/`manual_failed`); both mirrored verbatim. |
| **Atomic-ish design** | All rows computed in memory BEFORE the first UPSERT (mirrors 3.M-iii compute-before-write). Per-ticker fetch failures DO NOT propagate (`'error'` bar bundle → typed `fetch_error` row); one ticker NEVER crashes the run. UPSERT failure within a chunk returns `outcome:'failed'` with previously-written rows counted — partial write is by-chunk, not partial-within-row (every individual UPSERT is atomic on PostgREST's side). |
| **Mandatory pagination** | `combiner_book` + `combiner_book_shadow` + `combiner_forward_returns` (anti-join key) reads all go through `fetchAllRows` — page size 1000, short-read termination. A raw `.select()` on either book would silently truncate to ≤1000 seeds (the 3.0b-ii defect on `feature-assembler-orchestrator.ts`; ACT-237 corrective). |
| **Dedup-by-ticker** | Survivors are deduped to distinct tickers BEFORE the Polygon fan-out; one fetch per ticker even when (live × 12 shadow × {1,5,20}) tuples reference it. With ~480 book rows × 3 horizons before anti-join and ~200 distinct tickers per as_of, the per-run Polygon call count is ~200 — well within the existing budget that the daily signal stack already consumes. |
| **Maturation floor** | Pre-fetch pruning at `run_date − seed_as_of_date ≥ MATURATION_FLOOR_CAL_DAYS[H]` with `{1:1, 5:5, 20:20}`. H trading days always span ≥ H calendar days (a trading day IS a calendar day; weekends/holidays only widen the spread), so the floor never excludes a matured tuple. The bar array is the AUTHORITATIVE maturation check — the floor is an optimization, not a correctness gate. Explicitly NOT the `ceil(H × 1.45)` over-tight pre-filter (would exclude matured tuples in low-holiday windows). |
| **Wall-clock discipline** | `computed_at = as_of_run.toISOString()` per DEC-034 (4) — no `Date.now()` / `new Date()` anywhere in the orchestrator or accruer. Only `productionClock.getWallClockTs()` in the manual handler (sole sanctioned site for future-`as_of` rejection). |
| **`-999` sentinel discipline** | `accrueReturns` writes typed-absence as `NULL` on every non-success row (polygon_404, fetch_error, seed_bar_missing, horizon_bar_missing). Asserted by `acc-8` ("never emits -999 across all failure modes"). The `combiner_forward_returns_typed_absence_chk` CHECK would reject any -999 attempt at the DB layer regardless. |
| **Out-of-scope guarantees** | Zero edit to `PolygonPriceHistoryFetcher`, `momentum-orchestrator`, `shadow-ranker-orchestrator`, `ranker-orchestrator`, `feature-assembler-orchestrator`, or any live combiner code. Zero DB change. Zero `types.ts` regen. Zero cron / `job_registry` row (operator-invoked smoke only at 3.M-iv; cron is 3.M-v). NO write to `combiner_rankings_forward_returns` (deferred — does not exist; book-keyed forward returns are the 3.M-iv authoritative emission). |

No-auth POST probe `{"as_of":"2026-06-16"}` returned **401** — confirms the new edge fn is deployed and protected (would be 404 if the auto-deploy bridge had skipped first-commit enqueue per the twice-seen new-edge-fn pattern). |

(d) The operator cleanup SQL embedded in ACT-209 still applies to the stranded `aadb1329` run row (or DID, if the operator has already applied it — idempotent on the `status='running'` guard, so a re-application is a no-op now that the row has been flipped to `failed` either by the operator's cleanup SQL or by the run's own terminal-state landing at 21:29:28+00). |

### ACT-212: FP-050 Phase 4 — latent §(b) gap (Form-4 `index.json` missing `acceptanceDateTime`) — `readAcceptance` should consult SGML header as typed fallback (DEFERRED per ACT-211 operator ruling; OPEN — to be opened post-ACT-211 validation re-fire)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **ID** | ACT-212 (next-free after ACT-211; allocated as a stub-OPEN entry per ACT-211 operator ruling "(4) ACT-212 opens with C's deferred scope; latent §(b) gap on index.json-missing-acceptance — readAcceptance should consult SGML header as typed fallback; deferred to a focused follow-up, NOT bundled"). |
| **Mode** | OPEN — investigation + execution pending operator ruling AFTER the ACT-211 validation re-fire surfaces real `permanent_skip no_primary_doc` rates against the live universe. |
| **Status** | OPEN — DEFERRED. Not in-flight. Allocates work post-ACT-211 validation. |
| **Authority** | Operator 2026-06-13 ACT-211 ruling — "C deferred to ACT-212 (new entry; do not bundle)". |
| **Scope (proposed; subject to operator ratification when ACT-212 opens)** | (1) `edgar-accession-index-fetcher.ts`'s `readAcceptance(body)` currently consults four `acceptanceDateTime` / `acceptance-datetime` candidates inside `body` and `body.directory`. Live evidence (2026-06-13 EDGAR fetch of accession `0001058090-26-000045` for CMG/Chipotle): the modern Form-4 `index.json` shape for this filer (and likely a population of similar filers) carries NEITHER candidate, and the `acceptanceDateTime` is present ONLY in the `-index-headers.html` SGML wrapper at the same URL prefix. Under the current `readAcceptance` shape the fetcher returns `kind:'ambiguous', acceptance_datetime:null` even when a single `primary_document` resolved cleanly, and `processItem` routes to `permanent_skip no_primary_doc` — a clean terminal outcome but a coverage gap that suppresses real Form-4 rows. (2) Proposed fix: add a typed fallback that fetches `<accession-no-dashes>-index-headers.html` and extracts `<ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME>` from the SGML header when `index.json` lacks acceptance; the fetcher MUST stay typed (no silent string default) and the fallback fetch MUST count against the same SEC fair-access rate bucket. (3) New regression fixture: the Chipotle accession `0001058090-26-000045` real EDGAR shape (`index.json` + `-index-headers.html` content captured verbatim, no synthetic data). (4) Cost: at most one extra HTTP call per `index.json`-missing-acceptance filing; absent measurement of the population frequency, the bound is one extra call per processed item in the worst case (still inside the 5 rps fair-access ceiling). |
| **Blocking dependencies (registered per the deferred-work-register protocol)** | (a) ACT-211 must merge and the validation re-fire must produce live `signal_compute_log` evidence that confirms the §(b)-gap rate is material against the live universe (the (S.4) regression fixture proves the code-path; the live evidence proves the prevalence — only the latter justifies the implementation cost). (b) Operator ratification of the fix scope (single-fallback to SGML headers vs other shapes; rate-bucket accounting). |
| **References** | Authored at ACT-211 operator ruling. Referenced from ACT-211 Incidental Findings (a) and ACT-211 Status. Catalog cross-reference: §22.8.5 sub-class A (BUILD_SHA threading) and sub-class B (Registration-Dependency Deploy Gap) are unrelated — this is a §(b) (dual-date contract) coverage gap, not a deploy-pipeline gap. |
| **Verification Status** | N/A — entry is an OPEN stub. No code change, no test, no five-gate run, no deploy. Allocates work post-ACT-211 validation. |

| **Why PARK over BUILD (Option A) or INVESTIGATE (Option C)** | Build-once economics + risk profile. ### ACT-298 — insider-discovery post-write verification: PK-triple predicate (2026-06-18 red, Hypothesis A reconciled)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Date** | 2026-06-23 |
| **Mode** | EXECUTION (Tier A; verification-predicate fix only — write path unchanged) |
| **HEAD (pre)** | `a6e68260` |
| **Authority** | Supervisor; live-DB reconciliation (Claude + Lovable) of the 2026-06-23 GHA `insider-discovery` daily fire (correlation_id `dc50848f-2c54-4096-a38a-bb1d0f80e132`, `discovered_by=gha-daily`, `as_of=2026-06-18`) which exited 2 with `insider_discovery_supabase_failure: post-write verification found zero rows for discovery_correlation_id=dc50848f…` despite a 201 insert of 180 rows. Decisive ground-truth query: `SELECT as_of_date, discovery_correlation_id, count(*) FROM insider_accession_discovery_queue WHERE as_of_date='2026-06-18' GROUP BY …` → one row, **n=180**, correlation_id **`723b5f5d-744b-47bb-bf84-059bbab5b4cd`** (the 2026-06-20 run), discovered_at 2026-06-20 09:33:25 UTC; rows under `dc50848f…` = **0**. Confirms HYPOTHESIS A: benign idempotent re-run + verification-predicate bug. The 180 PK-triples all collided with the prior run's rows; `Prefer: resolution=ignore-duplicates,return=minimal` correctly suppressed every insert (201 with empty body — PostgREST gives no inserted-count signal under `return=minimal`). The old `verifyPersistedCount(env, thisRunCorrelationId)` predicate threw on zero because `ignore-duplicates` legitimately drops the new label on PKs that already exist — even though every accession this run discovered IS in the table, under the prior run's id. HYPOTHESIS B (real write hole) excluded by the live-DB query. |
| **Scope** | Verification-predicate replacement + log-key relabel + idempotent-re-run telemetry. EDITED 3 files: `scripts/insider-discovery-egress.ts` (added `verifyPersistedPkTriples` + `PkTriple`/`PkVerificationResult` exports; wrapped CLI inserter to capture submitted PK-triples; replaced the failure predicate from `persistedByCorrelation === 0` to `pkVerification.missing.length > 0`; renamed `rows_inserted → rows_submitted` in the run-complete log; added `submitted_pk_triples`/`present_after_verify`/`missing_after_verify`/`idempotent_rerun` log fields; positive `insider_discovery_idempotent_rerun` event emit on the benign-re-run path); `scripts/insider-discovery-egress_test.ts` (3 new hermetic tests `(c5a/b/c)`); this entry. NO write-path change (the `makeRestInserter` POST + `resolution=ignore-duplicates,return=minimal` is byte-unchanged). NO migration. NO schema change. NO cron arming. |
| **The fix — precise (not cheap) form** | `verifyPersistedPkTriples` asserts presence of every submitted `(as_of_date, issuer_cik, accession_number)` triple via per-day readback (`?select=issuer_cik,accession_number&as_of_date=eq.<day>` paged at 1000/page) intersected set-wise with the submitted day-bucket. SUCCESS iff every submitted triple is present **regardless of which `discovery_correlation_id` labels it** (a prior run's id is the same row). FAILURE only when a submitted triple is genuinely **missing** after the insert (the real write-hole / Hypothesis-B case the verification SHOULD catch). The cheaper "count by `as_of_date >= expected`" form was explicitly rejected per scope: it would pass if a DIFFERENT 180 rows existed for the day while these specific accessions were missing (partial-run masking). PK-triple intersect is bounded by per-day row count (~180/day in production) so URL-length is not a concern; pagination is in place for safety. |
| **Log relabel + telemetry** | `insider_discovery_run_complete`: `rows_inserted` → `rows_submitted` (PostgREST `return=minimal` gives no server-confirmed inserted-count, so the old name was a mislabel — the proximate source of the 2026-06-18 log self-contradiction); added `submitted_pk_triples`/`present_after_verify`/`missing_after_verify`/`idempotent_rerun` (booleans + counts derived from the new verifier); retained `persisted_rows_by_correlation_id` as diagnostic (zero with `present_after_verify == submitted` is now positively flagged as `idempotent_rerun=true`). New `insider_discovery_idempotent_rerun` event emits ONLY on the benign all-duplicates path (all submitted PKs present AND zero rows under this run's id AND expectedWrites > 0) so the next operator does not have to infer the benign case from log contradictions. Internal `DayOutcome.rows_inserted` field kept unchanged to bound test blast radius; the rename is on the JSON log keys (operator-facing). |
| **Tests** | 32 baseline `deno test scripts/insider-discovery-egress_test.ts` → all 32 green pre-change; **35 post-change, 35 green** (32 baseline + 3 new): `(c5a) verifyPersistedPkTriples: all submitted PKs present (benign idempotent re-run) → 0 missing` (pins the 2026-06-18 regression — the case that used to throw now passes), `(c5b) verifyPersistedPkTriples: a submitted PK genuinely missing (real write hole) → reported in missing[]` (pins the Hypothesis-B condition the new predicate MUST still catch), `(c5c) empty submitted set short-circuits` (no readback fetch when nothing was submitted). |
| **Live data state (post-diagnosis, pre-fix)** | `insider_accession_discovery_queue` for `as_of_date='2026-06-18'` = **180 rows present + intact** under correlation_id `723b5f5d-744b-47bb-bf84-059bbab5b4cd` (the 2026-06-20 first run). Zero rows under `dc50848f…`. The data pipeline was healthy throughout; the 2026-06-23 red was purely cosmetic-CI (the verification-predicate bug). No data recovery needed; the F2.c consumer (`seedWorkItems`) drains by `(as_of_date, consumed_at IS NULL)` — correlation_id is not part of its claim predicate, so the prior-id-labelled rows are claimable as normal. |
| **Out-of-scope guarantees** | Write path byte-unchanged: `makeRestInserter` POST + `Prefer: resolution=ignore-duplicates,return=minimal` + `insider_discovery_supabase_insert` event (with `attempted_rows` which is already accurately named) all unchanged. Zero migration / schema change. Zero touch to F2.c consumer / `insider-work-list-registration.ts` / `insider-queue-bootstrap.ts`. Zero cron arming. The legacy `verifyPersistedCount` helper retained for telemetry use (no longer load-bearing for the failure decision). |
| **Catalog crossing — POSTGREST `return=minimal` GIVES NO INSERTED-COUNT** | New forward-binding class (candidate Catalog entry on next firing): when a producer uses `Prefer: resolution=ignore-duplicates,return=minimal` against PostgREST, the response body is empty and there is NO server-side signal distinguishing "inserted N" from "inserted 0, suppressed N". Post-write verification MUST therefore assert **the intended natural-key presence**, NOT a count tagged by a per-run label that idempotent re-runs legitimately drop. Producers MAY log a submitted-count (with that exact name), but MUST NOT call it an inserted-count. This firing is single — the catalog row will be opened on the second firing per the §22.8.5 two-observation rule. |
| **ROI Impact** | Zero on prediction / signal / sizing / execution (the data was already present and correctly drainable by the consumer; the bug was in the CI exit code path, not the trading data). Positive on CI gate health (eliminates the benign-re-run false-fail class) and on diagnostic clarity (the next genuine write hole will surface with a precise `missing[N of M] (cik,accession)` message instead of an ambiguous zero-correlation-id message). |
| **Status** | Closed (ACT-298, 2026-06-23). |

Check (c) deno-cache-parse DEFERRED (re-invokes `deno cache` which is only safe under the 1.46.3 pin and largely duplicates the existing "Warm Deno cache" step; guards a hypothetical broken-v3-lock that has never occurred, whereas (a) guards the actual recurring clean-v5 class at zero risk via pure JSON read). |
| **Scope** | CREATED `scripts/check-lockfile-versions.ts` + `scripts/check-lockfile-versions_test.ts` (14 unit tests). UPDATED `docs/07-reference/function-index.md` (new entry under "Strong-evidence workflow tooling — sub-step 6.4 (ACT-082)" section, alphabetically between `check-audit-writer-trap` and `firing-diff`). NO touch to any other `check-*.ts` script. NO migration. NO cron arming. NO fire. |
| **Critical safety invariant — PURE JSON READ** | The script uses `Deno.readTextFile` + `JSON.parse` exclusively. It NEVER invokes `deno cache`, `deno test`, `Deno.run`, `Deno.Command`, or any subprocess. Under CI's pinned Deno 1.46.3 it is a true reader; under the Lovable sandbox's Deno 2.x it is ALSO a true reader — no module graph resolution against the registry, no lockfile rewrite path is reachable. This is the property that makes the gate safe to run anywhere: **it cannot itself trigger the v5 rewrite it guards.** Self-grep over the script confirms zero occurrences of `deno cache` / `Deno.run` / `Deno.Command` / `child_process` / `exec(` in code positions (the three matches are all in JSDoc prose explaining what the script does NOT do). |
| **Design** | Pure exports: `checkLockfileVersion(lockJson, path)` (sync; null = pass, typed `Violation` = fail with kind `wrong-version` / `missing-version-field`) + `checkLockfileAt(path, displayPath?)` (async I/O wrapper adding `missing-file` / `unparseable-json` kinds) + `checkAllLockfiles(rootDir?)` (iterates `REQUIRED_LOCKFILES = ['deno.lock', 'supabase/functions/deno.lock']`). `EXPECTED_LOCKFILE_VERSION = '3'` is a named constant pinned to CI's Deno 1.46.3 reader semantics per Catalog #58. `if (import.meta.main)` exits 0 on clean / 1 on any violation, with `console.error` per-violation message `"expected version "3"; a v5 lock is the DW-128 Deno-2.x-sandbox-vs-CI-1.46.3 divergence — regenerate at v3 per Catalog #58"`. Numeric `version: 3` is rejected — string equality required (defends against type drift). |
| **Verification** | (a) `deno test --allow-read --allow-write scripts/check-lockfile-versions_test.ts` → **14/14 green** (~49ms): v3-passes, v5-fails-with-observed=5, missing-version-field, non-object, numeric-version-rejected, missing-file, unparseable-json, tmp-fixture both-locks-pass, root-v5-only (exactly-one violation on root), functions-v5-only (exactly-one on functions), both-missing (two missing-file), REQUIRED_LOCKFILES contents, EXPECTED_LOCKFILE_VERSION pin, **current-repo CLEAN** (the production assertion). (b) `deno run --allow-read scripts/check-lockfile-versions.ts` against the live repo → `check-lockfile-versions: CLEAN — both lockfiles at version "3"` exit 0. (c) SHA-256 of `deno.lock` + `supabase/functions/deno.lock` byte-identical before vs after running the script + tests (root `59216bfd…`, functions `581b66ac…`) — the safety invariant holds empirically. (d) Self-grep confirms no `deno cache` / `Deno.run` / `Deno.Command` / `child_process` / `exec(` in code positions. |
| **Operator follow-up (out-of-scope here)** | (1) Author the early-CI-job `toolchain-parity` step in `.github/workflows/strong-evidence.yml` (first job or first steps before "Warm Deno cache"), invoking `deno run --allow-read scripts/check-lockfile-versions.ts` under the existing `setup-deno@v1 v1.46.3` pin. (2) Document the residual gap in DW-128 close-out: this is **prevention-via-fast-detection** (~60–120s into CI), NOT prevention-via-blocked-write — the committing environment (Lovable Deno 2.x sandbox) is structurally non-parity with CI and cannot self-check v3 without triggering the v5 rewrite. Zero-gap would require either a version-selectable Lovable runtime or PR-gated merges, both out of scope. |
| **Out-of-scope guarantees** | Zero `.yml` / `.github/` authoring (operator-gated). Zero `deno cache` invocation anywhere in the script. Zero touch to any other `check-*.ts` script. Zero touch to the existing lockfiles (verified byte-identical pre vs post). Zero migration / schema change / cron arming / model-artifact write / `FEATURE_ORDER` change. Inventory edit in `scripts/README.md` limited to one new row + a baseline-count caveat (no full inventory audit). |
| **ROI Impact** | Zero on prediction / signal / sizing / execution. Positive on CI gate health: the executable form of the thrice-firing Catalog #58 class is now in-tree and operator-runnable today (`deno run --allow-read scripts/check-lockfile-versions.ts`); once the operator wires the early-CI-job, every v5-lock regression fails fast (seconds) before the expensive Gates 1–15 run, instead of being caught mid-Gate-2 or later. |
| **Status** | Closed (ACT-299, 2026-06-23). |

### ACT-304 — CI red unblock: ban-ts-comment lint error on stub-capital-fetcher.ts (toolchain-parity Gate 0b)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Date** | 2026-06-24 |
| **Authority** | Supervisor (operator) — surface-fix only; no DEC, no schema, no config change. |
| **Branch base** | 74363581 (HEAD at start). |
| **Investigation (STEP A — config divergence claim REBUTTED)** | (1) **No CI/local divergence.** `.github/workflows/strong-evidence.yml` runs `npx eslint .` at Gate 0b (line 66) and Gate 4 (line 128) — the exact same invocation a developer runs locally. Both resolve `eslint.config.js` via ESLint's normal flat-config discovery; no `--config`, no `--no-eslintrc`, no alternate path. (2) **Why the other four sites did NOT fail #379.** `eslint.config.js` lines 27–37 set `"@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment": "off"` for a glob set: `**/*_test.ts`, `scripts/**/*.ts`, `**/test-fixtures.ts`, `src/features/longshort/services/broker/**/*.ts`. The catalyst `*_test.ts` sites match the first glob; `alpaca-paper-client.ts` matches the broker glob. `stub-capital-fetcher.ts` (under `supabase/functions/_shared/longshort-targets/`) matches NO override, so the default `tseslint.configs.recommended` ERROR level applies. The four other sites are genuinely out-of-scope of the rule and safe — no whack-a-mole. (3) **Is `@ts-expect-error` the correct standard?** Generally yes (it errors if the suppression becomes unnecessary), BUT it requires a real TS error on the next line — and `supabase/functions/**` is OUTSIDE `tsconfig.app.json`'s `include: ["src"]`, so tsc never typechecks this file in CI. The `declare const Deno: …` ambient declaration produces zero TS error in any CI gate. Per the operator STOP condition ("if the declare is error-free under CI's tsc, the directive should be DELETED, not converted"), the directive is removed. |
| **Scope landed** | EDIT `supabase/functions/_shared/longshort-targets/stub-capital-fetcher.ts` — replaced `// @ts-ignore — Deno global; consumed by edge runtime.` (line 38) with an explanatory non-directive comment block (no `@ts-*` directive). The `declare const Deno: …` line is preserved unchanged. NO other file touched. |

### ACT-308 — DEC-068 clause (j).2 + (j).3 wording reconciliation (code-aligned per §21.9 — episode-counting bound + worst-case envelope pinned)

| **Date** | 2026-06-24 |

Code-vs-DEC wording divergence surfaced at E1 verification (ACT-307 post-landing review): DEC-068 clause (j).2 wording said the per-side daily cap counts "RANK-POSITIONS-SCANNED, NOT candidates-accepted," but the landed code at `supabase/functions/_shared/longshort-execution/rebalance-planner.ts` (`selectFinalTargets`) counts SUBSTITUTION EPISODES (one same-side scan per failed primary slot; `MAX_SUBSTITUTION_ATTEMPTS_PER_SIDE_PER_DAY=10` bounds the number of slots that trigger a scan). Resolution (reconciled): align the DEC wording to the code. The code's episode-counting is the correct and superior bound for two reasons — (i) the "rank-positions-scanned" phrasing was written under the now-obsolete assumption that the kernel made live per-rank borrow-locate calls (per-rank API cost); clause (j).4's purity discipline made pre-flight results INJECTED, so there is NO per-rank I/O cost in the pure kernel and the position-counting rationale evaporated; (ii) literal position-counting would be a behavior regression — a single slot facing a wall of sector-illegal ranks 21–30 could exhaust the entire side budget and starve other failing slots, whereas episode-counting distributes the budget across failing slots. This is a wording-only amendment to clause (j).2 / (j).3 + the named-constants table footnote + an audit-facing worst-case-envelope addition. **NO code change, NO test change, NO migration, NO behavior change** — the code is correct; the DEC text is being aligned to it. |
